Title: N-able Takes N-central Platform Offline After Discovery of 33 Flaws
Critical RCE Vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server: Everything You Need To Know
Context: CVE-2026-119618 is a critical, high-severity vulnerability involving a race condition in the Apache HTTP Server, which was independently discovered by Anthropic and Google...
Full Text:
A critical synchronization vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618) has been identified in Apache HTTP Server’s HTTP/2 module (mod_http2). The flaw stems from a concurrent execution race condition within the assign_headers() function when handling shared resources. If successfully exploited, a remote, unauthenticated attacker can corrupt heap memory to achieve arbitrary code execution (RCE).

As of the time of this blog’s publication, no exploit is available and there are no reports of exploitation in the wild.

What is CVE-2026-111497?

CVE-2026-119618 is a critical, high-severity vulnerability involving a race condition in the Apache HTTP Server, which was independently discovered by Anthropic and Google Cloud’s Vulnerability Research Team.

Specifically, the flaw exists within the assign_headers() function of the HTTP/2 module (mod_http2). Due to improper synchronization when executing concurrent threads sharing resources, an attacker can trigger heap corruption. This memory corruption can ultimately be leveraged to achieve RCE on the hosting server, allowing unauthorized threat actors to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the web server process.

Wiz Research data: what’s the risk to cloud environments?

In cloud environments, a compromised Apache instance running containerized or virtualized workloads can serve as an entry point for lateral movement, potentially exposing adjacent microservices or cloud metadata endpoints.

According to Wiz data 64% of cloud environments have resources vulnerable to CVE-2026-119618, and 51% of cloud environments have publicly exposed instances. Note that this does not take configuration into account.

Which actions should security teams take?

Security operations and engineering teams should execute the following remediation and mitigation steps:

1. Upgrade Deployments

Upgrade Apache HTTP Server: Update affected installations to Apache HTTP Server version 2.4.71 or later. This release addresses the race condition in assign_headers().

Update Standalone Modules: If managing standalone mod_h2 builds from GitHub, upgrade the module to a version newer than 2.0.42.

2. Implement Temporary Mitigations

If immediate patching is not possible due to operational constraints, temporarily disable HTTP/2 support to eliminate the attack vector.

Edit the configuration file (such as httpd.conf) to restrict active protocols to HTTP/1.1 by removing h2 and h2c references:

# Restrict protocols to HTTP/1.1 Protocols http/1.1

Title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday November 2026, (Tue, Nov 10th)

One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing vulnerability in Outlook, is already being exploited.

Title: N-able Rushes Out N-central Fixes After 33 Zero-Days Go Public
Context: N-able has released a critical N-central hotfix that temporarily disables the platform's built-in remote control, after researcher Sean Bales published 33 alleged zero-days with...
Full Text:
N-able has released a critical N-central hotfix that temporarily disables the platform's built-in remote control, after researcher Sean Bales published 33 alleged zero-days with proof-of-concept (PoC) code.

N-able detailed N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2, build 2026.4.1.26, in its November 10 release notes, describing the update as a critical security release for its remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform.

The Able2Shell disclosure, published November 9, described four exploit chains that Bales said ended in code execution on an N-central server, two of them with root privileges and one he called credential-free. He said he tested the flaws on a pre-release build and that most if not all should work on earlier versions, including the current release.

Hotfix Covers Seven CVEs and Disables Remote Control

N-able took hosted N-central offline on November 9 as a precaution and told on-premises customers to keep their servers offline until they were updated.

Hotfix 2 addresses seven CVEs covering XML external entity (XXE) flaws, Object-Graph Navigation Language (OGNL) injection, privilege escalation, stored cross-site scripting, server-side request forgery and remote code execution through path traversal.

The seven records are CVE-2026-125883, CVE-2026-125878, CVE-2026-125879, CVE-2026-125880, CVE-2026-125881, CVE-2026-125882 and CVE-2026-91000. CVE-2026-125882 credits Nate Fair of Sprocket Security.

Remote control will be re-enabled in a future fix, according to the release notes, which also tell customers to update agents and probes after upgrading. N-able told Infosecurity that hosted environments have been upgraded and are back online.

N-able said the release addresses "the most critical November 9 vulnerabilities" and that a follow-up hotfix will bring further security updates.

Read more on N-central: N-able Releases Hotfix for Critical Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

N-able Disputes Disclosure as Exploitation Attempts Emerge

N-able said it was seeing scanning activity linked to the published PoC code.

Security firm WatchTowr saw exploitation attempts against its N-central honeypots overnight after the disclosure, according to an advisory updated November 10 by Beazley Security, the cybersecurity arm of insurer Beazley. The systems were decoys, not customer environments.

N-able said claims that it had ignored responsible disclosure from Bales were inaccurate, and that the vulnerabilities published on November 9 had not been disclosed through its established reporting channels.

Speaking to Infosecurity, Bales confirmed that N-able's account was accurate and that he had not disclosed any of the vulnerabilities to the company, adding that he believed the claim N-able had ignored him came from an outdated README he has since changed. He argued that publishing "makes vendors safer by forcing them to fix problems as fast as possible."

N-able president and CEO John Pagliuca took the opposite view, arguing that "publishing exploit code before customers have had the chance to act doesn't make anyone safer. It hands attackers a head start," he told Infosecurity.

Neither the release notes nor N-able's statement say how the seven CVEs map to the 33 Able2Shell issues, and PoC code for all 33 remains public.

Title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
Context: We thank Yuan Tan of NebuSec, who also independently found this vulnerability
Full Text:
In this article

From scans to reports

Selected findings

Closing thoughts

At Microsoft’s FORGE Lab, we used codename MDASH to scan a subset of Linux kernel subsystems from late May to mid-June 2026. One full-time researcher and one intern led this three-month effort, which has so far produced 59 public upstream reports and 33 assigned CVEs. We confirmed working root privilege-escalation exploits for eight of those CVEs, and fixes for 38 of our reports have been merged into mainline.

Finding the bugs was only part of the work. The initial scans produced 26,502 raw findings in about two weeks, but turning those results into reproducible bugs, upstream reports, and patches took months of expert investigation and collaboration with Linux maintainers.

In this post, we look back at how we went from thousands of potential findings to validated vulnerabilities and upstream fixes, and what we learned about scaling vulnerability discovery with AI.

From scans to reports

We focused on several core kernel subsystems, such as networking, filesystems, and security modules. Our selection criteria were straightforward: we picked security-sensitive components with no obvious dependence on specialized hardware, making QEMU-based validation simple and unified. Code scanning mainly used Sonnet 4.6 (71.1% of code-scanning tokens), GPT-5.4 (20.1%), and GPT-5.5 (7.1%).

The codename MDASH scans produced 26,502 raw scan findings in about two weeks on two servers (64 cores/256 GB RAM and 32 cores/128 GB RAM), but turning that output into patches and reports took months of expert work. We filtered out low-confidence claims using codename MDASH’s confidence levels and separate fast screening agents we built, reducing the pool to 11,769 candidates. PoC-generating agents then attempted reproduction in QEMU, mainly using GPT-5.5 (77.3% of reproduction tokens), Opus 4.6 (13.2%), and GPT-5.5-cyber (9.4%). Experts then reviewed the 621 cases with PoC evidence to identify root causes, merge duplicates, and prepare upstream submissions.

Figure 1 . Scan-to-report workflow. 26,502 raw findings → 11,769 screened candidates → 621 PoC-backed cases → 59 upstream reports.

Where the 621 cases went

Roughly one public upstream report landed from every ten PoC-backed cases: 59 reports from 621 cases (9.5%). Across those cases, the main reasons for not filing a separate new report were:

266 (42.8%) shared a root cause with another case, so one patch could fix them together.

163 (26.2%) were not reported after review, mostly due to limited security impact.

133 (21.4%) were already reported or fixed upstream.

Submission timing explains many of the 133 overlaps. Most of the 621 cases were new when the scans finished (though some may already have been in flight by others). Our first public report went out on June 27, 2026, more than five weeks after scanning started. By September 1, 55 of the 59 had been posted to the public lists; the other four were reported privately during the same window and routed to the public lists by mid-October.

Getting fixes merged

Upstream Linux typically requires vulnerability reports to come with a working patch. Agents helped draft initial fixes, but human validation, subsystem understanding, and iterating with maintainers during review remained essential. So far, fixes for 38 of our reports have been merged into upstream mainline—half on the first submission, and the rest after one to four revisions. Reaching a mainline release from the first public patch took a median of 41 days (up to 108 days), and we are still working with maintainers on the remaining reports.

How old the bugs were

Interestingly, most of the bugs we reported had been in the kernel for years. Across the 59 reports, the average bug was 8.1 years old when we first reported it publicly. One of the oldest, a cls_u32 shift-out-of-bounds bug (CVE-2026-74544), had been there for at least 21 years.

Figure 2 . Age of reported kernel bugs, measured from the bug-introducing commit (the fix’s Fixes tag) to our first public report. Average age 8.1 years across 59 reports; six were 15–19 years old and three were at least 20 years old.

Selected findings

Among the 33 CVEs assigned so far from this batch, 24 are rated High or above (CVSS v3.1 score of at least 7.0). Below are eight CVEs for which we confirmed local root privilege-escalation exploits in controlled laboratory environments, with some cases requiring non-default settings or disabled exploit mitigations:

CVE-2026-…

Module

Summary

64554

net/ipv6

Use-after-free in bridged IPv6 fragmentation: a saved pointer into a packet was reused after the packet’s buffer was reallocated.

64563

lib/rhashtable

Use-after-free in hash-table walks: a walk resumed after the table was resized reused a pointer to a possibly freed entry.

64580

net/ipv6

Refcount underflow in IPv6 IPsec routing: an error path dropped a device reference but kept the pointer, so cleanup dropped it again.

74561

net/ipv4

Use-after-free in next-hop replacement: the route-cache flush walked an IPv6 route list without its lock, racing with route deletion.

74562

net/ipv4

Use-after-free in next-hop replacement: route checks and notifications walked an IPv6 route list without its lock, racing with route deletion.

89789

drivers/net

Use-after-free in the GTP tunnel driver: when device creation failed, its lookup tables were freed while incoming packets could still read them.

98222

security/keys

Heap buffer overflow in encrypted-key updates: long key parameters overflowed a 16-bit length, so the kernel wrote past an undersized buffer.

98364

net/xfrm

Use-after-free in IPsec routing: a network device was used without holding a reference, so deleting it at the same time could free it mid-use.

A closer look at CVE-2026-64563

CVE-2026-64563 is a one-line state-reset bug in rhashtable, the Linux kernel’s shared resizable hash table. Because callers trust the object pointers returned by a table walk, this small library flaw enabled a stable local privilege escalation on Linux—and affected Android with SELinux enforcing—without requiring special kernel configurations or user namespaces.

Many kernel subsystems store live objects, such as sockets, in rhashtable and walk the table when user space asks to list them. Because a large listing may be split across several replies, a walk can pause and resume. Its iterator saves where it stopped, including a pointer to the last visited entry (iter->p). While the walk is paused, however, the table can still change: entries can be removed and freed, and resizing can replace the underlying bucket table.

The missed reset

Before 2018, rhashtable_walk_stop() always cleared iter->p = NULL on pause. To improve walk stability across stop/start cycles, a 2018 commit (5d240a8936f6) kept iter->p across walk_stop() and moved the reset into rhashtable_walk_start_check()—but only on one of its two resume paths:

Old table freed by a resize (iter->walker.tbl == NULL): lines 877–882 switch to the new table, reset slot and skip, and return -EAGAIN early without clearing iter->p:

Old table still present (iter->walker.tbl != NULL): lines 884–919 scan the bucket chain for iter->p and reset iter->p = NULL if the entry was removed.

if (!iter->walker.tbl) { iter->walker.tbl = rht_dereference_rcu(ht->tbl, ht); iter->slot = 0; iter->skip = 0; return -EAGAIN; }

After that restart, the next call to rhashtable_walk_next() sees iter->p still set and follows iter->p->next instead of starting over at slot = 0. If that entry was freed while the walk was paused, dereferencing iter->p->next reads from freed memory.

Why did this bug go unnoticed for eight years? Triggering it requires three conditions to line up in the same walk: the caller must pause and resume the same iterator across walk_stop() and walk_start(), a table resize must free the old bucket table during that pause, and the entry at iter->p must also be removed and freed before the walk resumes. Most rhashtable walkers finish in a single pass without ever resuming a stopped iterator, and even when a caller does pause and resume, those three events rarely coincide by accident in normal workloads.

The upstream fix simply clears the stale pointer before returning:

+ iter->p = NULL;

From a socket listing to a kernel write

Because rhashtable is a shared library, its callers determine both whether this bug is reachable and how severe its security impact can be. Across the kernel, there are about two dozen files that use the rhashtable walker API, and most walk the table in a single pass and immediately exit. Among those callers, we found two that pause and resume an iterator across batches and can at least cause a crash: TIPC’s socket dump (tipc_nl_sk_walk()) and Netlink’s socket diagnostics (__netlink_diag_dump()).

Of the two, __netlink_diag_dump() is the exploitable caller. It is reachable by unprivileged users on standard kernels, and user space controls the pause between dump replies (via recvmsg()). An attacker can hold a dump paused while resizing the table and freeing the socket at iter->p, then reallocate that memory to control iter->p->next—causing rhashtable_walk_next() to return a fake socket pointer sk.

__netlink_diag_dump() then checks net_eq(sock_net(sk), net) and passes sk to sk_diag_fill() and sock_diag_save_cookie(), which initializes sk->sk_cookie if it is zero. That turns the fake sk pointer into a constrained 64-bit write (when the target 8 bytes are zero and sk->sk_net matches &init_net). Paired with other general exploitation techniques, this write is enough for local privilege escalation.

We thank Yuan Tan of NebuSec, who also independently found this vulnerability. He promptly shared its real severity with us and the maintainers, which helped the upstream fix, and later provided us with his working exploits for both Linux and Android. We also thank Frank Wu of NebuSec, who identified a viable exploitation primitive and developed a working privilege-escalation exploit.

Closing thoughts

Finding bugs and fixing them are drastically out of balance. Two weeks of codename MDASH scanning produced the initial findings, which we narrowed to 621 PoC-backed cases. But it took over four person-months to report 59 of them—and five months later, 38 fixes have been merged. For complex infrastructure like the Linux kernel, keeping humans in the loop is still necessary, making human effort the bottleneck. Both bug hunters and maintainers can be overwhelmed by the volume of real findings, so focusing on genuinely high-severity issues is essential.

More tokens may yield more bugs, but not a secure system. We scanned only a small fraction of the kernel, and further tuning and more tokens could uncover substantially more bugs. But even after fixing all of them, is the system secure? At Microsoft FORGE Lab, we’re using AI to expand the scope of vulnerability research, but our experience shows that discovery is only one part of the work. The more urgent problem is how to build practical security solutions that are operational, cumulative, and economically sensible.

These lessons also extend beyond our research. Through close collaboration with the engineering teams building codename MDASH, we’re applying what we learn from real-world vulnerability discovery and validation to inform how these capabilities evolve. The goal is to bring advances in AI-powered security research into the hands of security teams, helping them identify and address critical vulnerabilities more effectively.

The post Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Title: Anthropic's Glasswing Finds Many Vulnerabilities Yet Delivers Few Fixes, Researcher Says
Context: The researcher added that since his last analysis of Glasswing vulnerability findings in September, Anthropic had added 4613 vulnerability findings to its ledger, yet only 15...
Full Text:
The researcher added that since his last analysis of Glasswing vulnerability findings in September, Anthropic had added 4613 vulnerability findings to its ledger, yet only 15 were marked as fixed within the same period. A significant volume of findings added to the ledger between September and November (1668) were marked as duplicates.

This led the researcher to question Anthropic’s latest claimed true positive rate of 94.2%, which, he said, raises “questions about how it accounts for duplicates and withdrawn findings.”

Read more: Anthropic Expands Mythos Access to 150 More Organizations

Anthropic Launched OSS Scanner to Scale Vulnerability Disclosures

One reason that could explain the gap between the vulnerabilities claimed to be found through Glasswing and vulnerabilities publicly fixed is the pace of human vulnerability report triage.

On October 8, Anthropic said it had found more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities but had manually reviewed only about 6000, and that it remains "bottlenecked on our human capacity to validate these findings."

“We are working on scaling our vulnerability disclosures,” the company added.

Therefore, it launched its own Open Source Security Scanner (OSS Scanner), a self-service new tool inspired by Google's OSS-Fuzz project and that allows maintainers to request a scan and triage the findings themselves.

Anthropic also said it has already sent nearly 5000 unverified vulnerability reports directly to maintainers who asked to receive everything in bulk.

This new shift in Project Glasswing started showing issues in AI-powered vulnerability reports more clearly.

For instance, Daniel Stenberg, maintainer of the Client and URL (cURL) project, said on November 6 he received 45 vulnerability reports from Anthropic through Glasswing.

After analyzing 34 of them using Anthropic OSS Scanner and other tools, Stenberg pointed out that 19 weren't vulnerabilities at all and six have been confirmed as low severity.

“AI is a valuable tool for finding vulnerabilities, and I'm not discounting that. But seven months in, the evidence still doesn't match the launch narrative. The CVEs are a sliver of this year's total, almost none are being exploited, fixes have stalled while duplicates and withdrawals pile up, and the triage burden is shifting onto the open source maintainers Glasswing promised to help. The receipts keep coming in. They still don't reconcile,” Garrity concluded.

Infosecurity contacted Anthropic for comment, but the company had not responded by the time of publication.

Title: Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks
Context: A threat actor has been exploiting a critical-severity authentication bypass and a zero-day in Xen Orchestra, software maker Vates warns
Full Text:
A threat actor has been exploiting a critical-severity authentication bypass and a zero-day in Xen Orchestra, software maker Vates warns.

A web-based backup, management, and disaster recovery solution for XCP-ng and XenServer virtualization environments, Xen Orchestra operates as an agentless control center across hosts, VMs, storage, and pools.

The critical flaw exists in the REST authentication mechanism, where an authentication token is turned into {} and then treated as an unfiltered lookup, leading to the first token being returned by token collection. If the token is not expired, the provider authenticates as its owner.

This opens a route that exposes reusable login token IDs, allowing unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrator privileges.

“Xen Orchestra compromise can lead to arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root,” Vates says.

The security defect impacts Xen Orchestra releases before 6.9.2 (stable) and 6.10.1 (latest), and Xen Orchestra Appliance, which contains Xen Orchestra.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Vates warned that the same threat actor has been exploiting this bug and a zero-day vulnerability that requires administrator privileges. The zero-day allows malicious VM imports that could compromise XCP-ng hosts, and a fix is still being developed.

According to the company, the attacker initially operated from 91.211.251.112:8001 and via the Tor network. No CVE identifier has been assigned to the security defects.

The company warns that unauthorized access is not logged, but has shared indicators of compromise (IoCs) associated with the observed attacks, and warns that they are limited to this specific campaign.

“Exploitation of the vulnerability by other threat actors using different TTPs and infrastructure cannot be ruled out. The absence of these IoCs alone is not sufficient to conclude that no compromise has occurred,” Vates notes.

The company recommends placing Xen Orchestra instances behind a dedicated network, blocking IP addresses and domain names associated with known malicious activity, blocking the empty token in a WAF rule, and rotating all potentially compromised credentials.

“In case of a confirmed compromise, a full reinstallation is recommended as cleanup alone cannot guarantee the removal of all backdoors left by the attacker,” Vates says.

Title: Git fixes six vulnerabilities, including code execution during recursive clones
Context: The Git project has released security updates addressing six vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to execute code, write to unintended files or cause memory corruption...
Full Text:
The Git project has released security updates addressing six vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to execute code, write to unintended files or cause memory corruption when Git processes malicious repositories or other specially prepared input.

Code execution during cloning

A vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-111760 stems from an integer truncation in Git’s handling of its index. An extremely long file path can pass Git’s safety checks under one name and then be written under a shorter one.

By exploiting this discrepancy, an attacker can replace a submodule’s .git file with a symbolic link pointing to a directory containing malicious configuration or hooks. This can cause attacker-controlled code to run during a recursive clone. The fix rejects overly long index paths before their lengths can be truncated.

Five more vulnerabilities

When cloning an empty repository over v2 protocol, Git did not validate the target of the HEAD symbolic reference that a server advertised, so a malicious server could therefore use path-traversal components to make a subsequent branch update, with the files reference backend, write outside the intended reference directory. Git now validates that target, along with other reference names and symbolic-reference targets received over protocol v2, closing the hole identified as CVE-2026-113408.

Git’s code for stripping GPG signatures assumed a message held at most two signatures. A crafted message with more can overflow a fixed-size stack array, causing memory corruption or a crash, for example when someone merges a specially crafted tag. Hosting services that perform merges on behalf of users may be exposed, according to the advisory for CVE-2026-114467.

CVE-2026-114469 concerns binary patches. Git’s roughly 1 GiB limit on patch size checked only the size of the patch as supplied, so a small patch could expand past the limit when decoded and trigger an out-of-bounds read and a crash. Git now also checks the declared uncompressed size before processing.

CVE-2026-105437 affects Git’s merge machinery, where a memory-size calculation can overflow on very large results, such as many conflicts combined with a large conflict-marker-size attribute. This can cause Git to allocate a buffer that is too small and corrupts heap memory. Both local merges and services that merge untrusted content are affected.

The sixth flaw, CVE-2026-114466, affects git fast-import. Three features lacked safeguards when supplied through untrusted input streams. Two submodule-rewriting options could read arbitrary files, potentially leaking contents through error messages, while a third could create or append to files. Unless the caller explicitly allows unsafe features, they are rejected when supplied through the input stream. GitHub advises enabling that option only when the program generating the stream is trusted.

GitHub’s response

The patches ship in Git 2.56.1, with backports for the 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3 and 2.50.2 series. Maintainers recommend that users update to 2.56.1 or the patched release for their series, and that they also update any software that bundles its own copy of Git.

GitHub said it has deployed fixes across github.com, GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency.

GitHub Enterprise Server administrators are advised to upgrade promptly to version 3.19.15, 3.20.11, 3.21.9 or 3.22.4. Patched Git builds are being coordinated for GitHub Desktop and the GitHub Copilot app, and GitHub Codespaces and GitHub Actions will also receive them.

What should users do

Users should install a patched Git from their operating system or Git distributor, and administrators should also update Git on automation and services that process repositories on behalf of others.

“If you cannot update immediately, clone only from trusted servers and avoid recursive clones of untrusted repositories. Avoid merging untrusted content or tags, or processing binary patches or fast-import streams from untrusted sources. These precautions do not replace installing the fixes,” Elijah Newren, Staff Software Engineer at GitHub, said.

Full Text:
Threat actors have been observed targeting Qlik Sense servers to unsuccessfully deliver PowerShell reverse shell commands against multiple environments in October 2026.

Cynet's CyOps and Research teams said they identified the suspicious activity in October 2026 against several E.U.-based customers within a narrow window of just over three minutes.

The activity has been found to share some level of overlap with a November 2023 campaign documented by Arctic Wolf in which threat actors linked to the CACTUS ransomware operation likely weaponized then-newly-disclosed flaws in Qlik Sense to obtain initial access to target environments.

The vulnerabilities in question, which were patched by Qlik Sense in August and September 2023, impact Qlik Sense Enterprise for Windows -

CVE-2023-41265 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An HTTP tunneling vulnerability that could lead to privilege escalation and allow an attacker to execute HTTP requests on the backend server hosting the repository application.

CVE-2023-41266 (CVSS score: 8.2) - A path traversal vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to generate an anonymous session and perform HTTP requests to unauthorized endpoints.

CVE-2023-48365 (CVSS score: 9.6) - An unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability that stems from improper validation of HTTP headers, allowing an attacker to elevate their privilege by tunneling HTTP requests and execute HTTP requests on the backend server.

It's worth noting that CVE-2023-48365 (aka DoubleQlik) is an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-41265.

In November 2023 CACTUS ransomware campaign, threat actors were observed exploiting the flaws to establish a foothold and download additional payloads to establish persistence and remote control by deploying ManageEngine Unified Endpoint Management and Security (UEMS), AnyDesk, and Plink.

The latest activity detected by Cynet involves the use of a PowerShell command containing a one-line reverse shell that connects to "45.115.26[.]23" on port 4455. The exact vulnerability exploited to break into Qlik Sense servers is currently not known.

"The command was executed under scheduler.exe, resembling the 2023 Cactus Qlik intrusions," the cybersecurity company said.

Although attempts to spawn the reverse shell were blocked, Cynet's testing of the reverse shell in a controlled environment has revealed that the interactive communication channel is used to conduct reconnaissance and deliver a PowerShell script for enabling persistence.

This is achieved by means of a Windows Go reverse shell that connects to "45.115.26[.]23:4456." The backdoor is then used to look for actively running processes related to Apache ActiveMQ. On Linux, the malware also attempts to collect system information and read "/etc/shadow" and "/etc/passwd" files.

A second variant of the PowerShell script attempts to install OpenSSH and creates a scheduled task named "WinUpdCheck" that launches a PowerShell reverse shell written to "C:\ProgramData\ssh\winc.ps1" at five-minute intervals.

"If sshd remained unavailable, it downloaded OpenSSH-Win64.zip from the staging server, extracted it, and ran install-sshd.ps1," Cynet said. "It set sshd to automatic startup, started the service, and added an inbound firewall rule for TCP 22. The archive was a legitimate OpenSSH package reused by the operator."

Further analysis of the infrastructure has uncovered an exposed directory ("45.115.26[.]23:8012") consisting of a custom Go backdoor for Windows, SSH persistence scripts, an ActiveMQ exploit for CVE-2023-46604, and a modified public Veeam toolchain for CVE-2024-40711, indicating the threat actor is possibly laying the groundwork for broader attacks.

Title: Asus, Zoom Release Security Patches
Context: Successful exploitation of the flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges or overwrite memory and cause a crash
Full Text:
Asus and Zoom are among the tech companies that have released fresh security updates for their products this week.

Computer maker Asus published an advisory describing four high- and medium-severity vulnerabilities in certain router firmware releases.

Successful exploitation of the flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges or overwrite memory and cause a crash.

Zoom has patched two vulnerabilities in Workplace for Windows, including a critical-severity unauthenticated privilege escalation bug tracked as CVE-2026-108186 (CVSS score of 9.6).

The second issue (CVE-2026-108187, CVSS score of 8.1) could also allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to elevate their privileges.

Zoom Workplace for Windows versions 7.1.8 and later contain patches for both bugs. Zoom makes no mention of any of these flaws being exploited in the wild.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Additionally, Cisco updated several advisories: it added fresh information on Node2Shell’s impact and on an authorization bypass’s impact on ISE and ISE-PIC, and added new details on the availability of fixes for seven critical- and high-severity CVEs in Meraki products.

On Tuesday, both Cisco and SonicWall announced they have removed root certificates affected by compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates.

The fresh security updates arrived among hundreds of patches from Apple, Fortinet, Citrix, Ivanti, Intel, AMD, Microsoft, Adobe, SAP, and multiple ICS vendors.

Title: Citrix, Ivanti Patch Critical and High-Severity Vulnerabilities
Context: Citrix and Ivanti on Tuesday announced patches for 19 vulnerabilities in their products, including multiple critical- and high-severity flaws
Full Text:
Citrix and Ivanti on Tuesday announced patches for 19 vulnerabilities in their products, including multiple critical- and high-severity flaws.

Ivanti fixed 13 vulnerabilities across five products, including two critical-severity defects in Cloud Services Application (CSA) and Endpoint Manager (EPM).

Tracked as CVE-2026-121683 (CVSS score of 9.4), the CSA flaw is described as a missing authentication issue that could allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to “add and delete arbitrary trusted EPM Core certificate entries”.

CSA version 5.0.8.1 patches the bug. Deployments running with a Dual NIC configuration cannot be exploited externally, Ivanti notes.

The critical EPM issue, tracked as CVE-2026-121653 (CVSS score of 9.8), is an SQL injection bug that could lead to remote code execution (RCE) without authentication.

It was resolved in EPM version 2024 SU8, which also addresses a medium-severity cleartext transmission of sensitive information exploitable via MitM attacks.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Ivanti released patches for four vulnerabilities in Sentry, including a high-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaw. Tracked as CVE-2026-105425, the bug was also fixed in Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM), along with five medium-severity issues.

On Tuesday, the company also addressed a medium-severity defect in User Workspace Manager (UWM). Ivanti says it has no evidence of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild.

Citrix rolled out fixes for six security defects in XenServer, including CVE-2026-102705, a high-severity bug that could allow attackers to infer the Pool Secret and compromise the host.

The remaining five issues could lead to privilege escalation or could allow administrators with any role to terminate the running tasks of other roles.

Additionally, Citrix released XenServer updates that mitigate several AMD CPU vulnerabilities that could allow guest VMs to compromise the host or infer the active memory content of another VM.

Title: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities
Context: While N-able has yet to flag these flaws as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that attackers have already started scanning the Internet...
Full Text:
N-able released hotfixes to address zero-day bugs affecting its N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, which were publicly disclosed over the weekend and forced it to take vulnerable hosted environments offline.

This follows N-able's decision to take all hosted N-central environments offline across the Americas, Europe, and Asia-Pacific regions until it could patch them against potential attacks targeting the zero-day flaws in the wild.

"N-able is actively responding to non-responsible communication of critical vulnerabilities in N-central late Sunday night, November 8, found by an independent researcher," N-able told BleepingComputer on Monday. "As a precautionary measure, we took our Hosted N-central environment offline today, November 9, and provided guidance to customers operating on-premises N-central servers to temporarily take their servers offline until further notice."

N-central lets IT departments and managed service providers (MSPs) monitor, manage, and maintain client networks and devices from a centralized web-based console.

N-able has now released N-central 2026.4 HF2 with security patches and technology updates for some of the leaked zero-days, including "the most critical" vulnerabilities:

CVE-2026-125883 - Multiple XXE Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125878 - Multiple OGNL Injection vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125879 - Local privilege escalation to root via nable-writable syslog-ng config

CVE-2026-125880 - Stored XSS via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)

CVE-2026-125881 - Schema-hint SSRF via service import schema validation

CVE-2026-125882 - RCE via file repository upload path traversal (Credit Nate Fair, Sprocket Security)

CVE-2026-91000 - Insecure IPC Channels lead to local privilege escalation

In a Tuesday update, N-able said that all hosted N-central servers (NCODs) across all regions have now been successfully upgraded and advised and "strongly" recommended that all N-central On-Premises customers upgrade their installations to the newly released version "as soon as possible."

"Customers should follow the published upgrade guidance carefully before restoring normal access to their N-central environment. Earlier incident guidance advised On-Premises customers to keep their N-central servers offline while remediation was being developed," it said.

While N-able has yet to flag these flaws as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that attackers have already started scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems and warned admins to take N-central servers offline immediately.

"During the past 24 hours, we have observed probing of N-able N-central for the 0-days that were dropped publicly yesterday," Defused said. "We have seen opening of anonymous agent sessions, pulling appliance config and hitting the remote control endpoint without auth. These pathways are part of the 0-day exploit surface."

Internet security nonprofit Shadowserver reports that just over 148 N-central servers are currently exposed online, a sharp decrease from the 1,338 it detected on Monday.

Disclosed after previous reports were allegedly ignored

Security researcher Sean Bales disclosed the vulnerabilities late Sunday, November 8, and published a GitHub repository called Able2Shell containing proof-of-concept exploits for the flaws.

Bales said the zero-day bugs affect N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31, a pre-release version of the software, and believes that most (if not all) of the flaws also affect earlier versions.

The disclosed vulnerabilities include remote code execution (RCE), authentication bypasses, credential disclosure, arbitrary file writes, directory traversal, XML external entity (XXE) injection, and cross-site scripting (XSS) flaws.

The security researcher also demoed a critical unauthenticated XXE-to-RCE exploit chain that abuses N-central's service-import functionality to steal a trusted local session, reset the targeted account's password, and execute commands on the server as the nable user.

Attackers could also use this exploit to create a Default Administrator account with attacker-controlled credentials, which provides them rogue admin access to the N-central management interface, as shown in the video demo embedded below.

Bales told BleepingComputer that he released the N-central zero-days without notifying N-able because the company allegedly failed to patch vulnerabilities (including two unrelated remote code execution bugs and a privilege-escalation flaw) he reported in a different N-able product about five to six months ago.

When asked about Bales' allegations regarding the previously disclosed security issues, N-able did not address the questions and instead responded with a statement about the N-central security incident and precautionary shutdown.

N-able provides cloud-based remote monitoring, cybersecurity, and data protection tools for Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and enterprise IT departments at more than 500,000 organizations in over 140 countries.

Title: Fortinet Patches Nearly 100 Vulnerabilities
Context: Approximately 17 of the newly resolved flaws are critical-severity issues, several of which could be exploited for arbitrary code execution
Full Text:
Fortinet on Tuesday dropped 89 new security advisories that address nearly 100 vulnerabilities across its products.

The massive release comes three weeks after the company announced it has integrated frontier AI models into its product security testing and can discover security defects more efficiently.

“This ongoing effort complements the conventional methods we employ to identify and address vulnerabilities. This approach gives customers time to prioritize upgrades before additional technical details become public, which matters even more as AI shortens the time between disclosure and exploitation,” Fortinet says.

Approximately 17 of the newly resolved flaws are critical-severity issues, several of which could be exploited for arbitrary code execution.

Other critical bugs could lead to authentication bypass, LSA broadcast, account takeover, access to other VDOMs and to secure email accounts, IBE webmail session compromise, server-side request execution, malicious/malformed attribute delivery, webmail password resets, and command execution as super admin.

FortiMail received the largest batch of critical fixes, followed by FortiAuthenticator, FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer. New FortiSASE and FortiClient updates also resolve critical issues.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

According to Baldur Security principal security consultant Kevin Joensen, the FortiClient bug is exploitable if FortiPAM is enabled and could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code if the victim visits a malicious website.

“The root cause is a CORS misconfiguration that allows attacker-controlled web pages to communicate with a local service and reliably execute arbitrary code,” Joensen says. The researcher named the flaw Fortinet2Shell.

Fortinet also patched nearly 80 high-severity vulnerabilities that could lead to XSS attacks, code execution, code injection, arbitrary file uploads, command execution, denial-of-service (DoS) conditions, MitM attacks, privilege escalation, information disclosure, account takeover, unauthorized access, and other unauthorized actions.

Fortinet makes no mention of any of these security defects being exploited in the wild. Additional information can be found on the company’s PSIRT page.

Title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday fixes Outlook flaw already under attack
Context: We’ll start with CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook vulnerability that attackers are already exploiting
Full Text:
Microsoft’s November Patch Tuesday fixes more than 1,000 Microsoft vulnerabilities, including an Outlook flaw that attackers are already exploiting to steal authentication information.

The release also fixes 48 critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to run code on affected machines, in some cases without user interaction.

While Windows updates address many of this month’s vulnerabilities, readers should check for Office updates as well: the exploited Outlook flaw is patched through the affected Office products.

To do this, follow these instructions:

Open an Office application, such as Word.

Go to File > Account. In Outlook, this may appear as Office Account.

Under Product Information, select Update Options > Update Now.

If necessary, select Enable Updates first. If the update controls are missing on a work device, contact your organization’s IT team; updates may be centrally managed.

During the update, you may be prompted to save your work (check your open documents). Afterward, you should see something similar to this:

Office updates installed

How to apply Windows patches and check if you’re protected

These updates fix security problems and help keep your Windows PC protected. Here’s how to make sure you’re up to date:

Click the Start button, then open Settings.

Select Windows Update (usually at the bottom of the menu on the left).

Click Check for updates. Windows will search for the latest security updates. If you’ve enabled Get the latest updates as soon as they’re available under More options, you may be prompted to restart immediately to complete the update.

You may find the update (Security Update KB5132061) already installed.

Windows Update history

If updates are available, they’ll start downloading automatically. When they’re ready, click Install or Restart now if prompted. Your computer may need a restart to finish the update.

After restarting, go back to Windows Update and check again. If it says You’re up to date, you’re all set.

Technical details

As usual, we’ve selected a few vulnerabilities to highlight for readers interested in the technical details.

We’ll start with CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook vulnerability that attackers are already exploiting. It has a CVSS score of 6.5 out of 10 and could expose authentication information that attackers could use to impersonate the user. From Microsoft’s description:

“Product ui does not warn user of unsafe actions in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.”

To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker must convince someone to open a specially crafted message file in an affected version of Outlook. This can cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without its usual external-content warning, potentially exposing authentication information (the user’s NTLMv2 hash) that could be used to impersonate them.

As this vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, updating Office as described earlier is a priority.

One other vulnerability I want to highlight is CVE-2026-116928 (CVSS score 9.8 out of 10):

“Out-of-bounds write in Microsoft Windows Search Component allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.”

An out-of-bounds write vulnerability allows a program to write outside the memory boundaries it is supposed to use, which can lead to memory corruption or place malicious code in memory and trick the system into running it.

Microsoft describes an attack in which a malicious email attachment is processed automatically for indexing by Exchange Server. In that scenario, the recipient does not need to open the email or attachment. Processing it could be enough to let the attacker run code with the permissions of the affected service. Microsoft has not reported exploitation of this vulnerability.

Title: Microsoft fixes audio issues caused by September security updates
Context: " errors in Device Manager, while others said the impacted USB audio speakers fail only when using multichannel audio features, including 3D audio or 8-channel modes
Full Text:
Microsoft says the November 2026 cumulative updates resolve USB audio issues plaguing Windows users who have installed security updates released since September.

The company explained, when it acknowledged this known issue days after the September 2026 Patch Tuesday, that USB Audio Class 1.0 devices failed to start or produce audio on some systems after installing recent updates.

Some affected users reported seeing no audio output, unresponsive volume controls and sound settings, and "This device cannot start (Code 10)." errors in Device Manager, while others said the impacted USB audio speakers fail only when using multichannel audio features, including 3D audio or 8-channel modes.

These audio issues affect both server (Windows Server 2012 and later) and client (Windows 10 and Windows 11) systems.

Microsoft released out-of-band updates on September 14 to fix the symptoms experienced on devices using 8-channel or 3D audio modes and has now addressed the remaining issues in security updates released as part of this month's Patch Tuesday.

"The symptoms are resolved in the Windows security update released on November 10, 2026 (KB5132061) and later updates," Microsoft said in a Windows release health dashboard update.

"We recommend you install the latest security update for your device as it contains important improvements and issue resolutions, including this one."

While Microsoft has yet to provide an official workaround for those who can't immediately install the November 2026 security updates, some users have restored audio on affected Windows PCs by switching to 2-channel mode.

Previous audio issues affecting Windows systems

Two years ago, Microsoft also confirmed an issue that caused game audio to unexpectedly increase to full volume when using USB DAC sound systems and blocked Windows 24H2 upgrades on systems with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio drivers due to blue screen of death (BSOD) issues.

In January 2025, Microsoft addressed a similar issue triggered by the KB5050094 optional preview cumulative update, which caused audio playback issues and Code 10 errors on Windows 11 24H2 systems with USB audio device drivers.

More recently, in September 2025, it lifted a safeguard hold preventing Windows 11 24H2 upgrades on systems with Dirac audio improvement software because compatibility issues caused Bluetooth speakers and headsets to malfunction.

With the November 2026 cumulative updates, Microsoft also resolved Outlook sign-in and mail delivery issues on Exchange Server systems triggered by the October 2026 Windows Server security updates.

Title: ICS Patch Tuesday: Siemens Flags High-Severity Flaws, Node2Shell Exposure
Context: Exploitation attempts of Node2Shell have been spotted, but there is no indication of attacks specifically targeting Siemens products
Full Text:
Siemens, Schneider Electric, and several other industrial technology vendors have published new security advisories describing vulnerabilities that could expose affected systems to serious attacks.

Siemens has published nine new advisories covering 10 vulnerabilities. Two advisories describe the impact of the recent Node2Shell vulnerability on the company’s products. Exploitation attempts of Node2Shell have been spotted, but there is no indication of attacks specifically targeting Siemens products.

Siemens has also published advisories informing customers about high-severity vulnerabilities in ROS#, Simcenter Femap, Mendix Studio Pro MCP Server, Simatic SCADA and PCS 7, Meta-iot2050, and Simatic WinCC Graphics Designer. The flaws can be exploited to inject code, execute arbitrary code, access unauthorized data, and compromise the system.

Siemens says patches are not yet available for several affected products, and some versions will not receive fixes. Customers are advised to apply the recommended mitigations.

Schneider Electric has published only one advisory informing customers about a medium-severity issue in EcoStruxure Power Build Rapsody that could be exploited for arbitrary code execution by processing malicious files.

Title: CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks
Context: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks
Full Text:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks.

Cisco BroadWorks is a cloud unified communications (UC) software platform and the underlying engine allowing telecom carriers and managed service providers (MSPs) to provide branded cloud PBX, voice, and collaboration services to business customers.

Tracked as CVE-2026-20320, the security flaw stems from an improper restriction of XML External Entity (XXE) reference weakness in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser that can allow unauthenticated, remote attackers to read sensitive configuration information from vulnerable systems by sending maliciously crafted XML messages.

"This vulnerability exists because XML entries are improperly parsed due to external entity resolution being allowed by default. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted XML message to the Open Client Interface - Provisioning (OCI-P) service," Cisco explained when it patched the bug in August.

CISA flagged CVE-2026-20320 as actively exploited and added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday, ordering Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within two weeks, by November 24, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.

Although BOD 26-04 targets only federal agencies, CISA urged all security teams, including those in the private sector, to prioritize patches for this vulnerability to defend their networks against ongoing attacks.

"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise," it warned. "While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities."

Targeted in autonomous AI attack

While CISA didn't share more details on attackers exploiting CVE-2026-20320 in the wild, threat intelligence firm Malbear Labs said over the weekend that a Chinese-speaking threat actor has exploited the flaw with the help of a jailbroken DeepSeek Flash artificial intelligence model in attacks targeting a European telecommunications provider and thirteen organizations that used its data centers and cloud infrastructure.

The attack focused on the telecom provider's BroadWorks XSP (eXtended Services Platform), and Malbear Labs found that the BroadWorks Provisioning Server (which stores subscriber configuration for all users) was also exposed via an unauthenticated directory listing.

"The agent exploited CVE-2026-20320, an unauthenticated XXE in the BroadWorks OCI XML parser. A crafted OCI request to port 2208 causes the XML parser to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem and no prior authentication required," Malbear Labs said.

"From the XSP host, the agent recovered the system identity private key, three SSL credential sets, and three additional private keys with certificate matches confirmed. The system identity key is used by the BroadWorks platform to authenticate between its own components; possessing it allows impersonation of the XSP in inter-component communication."

Since November 2021, CISA has added 103 Cisco vulnerabilities to its list of actively exploited flaws, seven of which have also been abused by ransomware gangs.

Title: Microsoft Fixes 1235 Flaws in Another Record Patch Tuesday
Context: The zero-day vulnerability is CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing bug in Microsoft Outlook, exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes
Full Text:
Microsoft has issued updates to fix over 1200 vulnerabilities in its products, a new record.

The tech giant’s November Patch Tuesday contained fixes for 1235 flaws, including one zero-day being actively exploited in the wild.

It makes this month the fourth this year in which Microsoft has issued a record number of patches, following previous milestones passed in July, September and October.

The zero-day vulnerability is CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing bug in Microsoft Outlook, exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes.

“An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and gets the user to open it. Outlook then connects to a network location the attacker controls, but it skips the usual warning about external content,” explained Action1 director of vulnerability research, Jack Bicer.

“That quiet connection can leak the user's NTLMv2 hash, a scrambled form of their login secret, which the attacker can use to sign in as that person. It affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and Office LTSC 2021 and 2024.”

Read more on patching: Exploited Vulnerabilities Typically Take Three Months to Patch, Moody’s Finds

Although the zero-day is rated “moderate,” sysadmins should prioritize it, Bicer advised.

“Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs,” he added. “A stolen hash can open doors far beyond the inbox. Push the Office update to every Outlook user now, starting with administrators and high-value accounts.”

The majority (536) of CVEs patched this month are elevation of privilege (EoP), followed by remote code execution (296) and information disclosure (157).

A total of 66 are rated critical, most of these being remote code execution flaws.

SAP Patch Volumes Hit New Highs

Microsoft wasn’t the only software giant to release a record-breaking number of security updates yesterday. SAP’s November Patch Day was the biggest ever, with 43 vulnerabilities addressed, including 12 Hot News Notes and 13 High Priority.

“Hot News” is the highest priority ranking given to SAP security updates (Notes).

The patch load was twice the size of the average for 2026 and included four with a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, according to Onapsis.

These were:

CVE-2026-89103 (SAP Security Note #3798345), a broken access control vulnerability in SAP Gateway dubbed “ProxyGate”

CVE-2026-76964 (SAP Security Note #3778530), a memory corruption flaw in SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP (Internet Communication Manager)

CVE-2026-89126 (SAP Security Note #3778556), a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP Web Dispatcher

CVE-2026-120017 (SAP Security Note #3849308), a missing authentication (SAML2 authentication bypass) vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP and ABAP Platform (SAML2 Service Provider)

Title: Microsoft November Patch Tuesday: one exploited Outlook bug and 30 wormable flaws
Context: CVE-2026-119952, a Schannel remote code execution flaw, is marked “Exploitation More Likely”, one of only a few Critical patches with that rating, and its high attack complexity...
Full Text:
Microsoft November Patch Tuesday security updates fix 1,090 flaws, including one exploited Outlook bug and 30 potentially wormable issues.

Microsoft November Patch Tuesday addressed about 1,090 new vulnerabilities, which is less than the roughly 1,400 last month. Two months in a row now exceed every previous year from Microsoft, and the overall count is a bit confusing, so other trackers report different totals.

The release covers Windows and its components, Office, networking and remote access, graphics, media and printing, storage and file systems, .NET and Visual Studio, security and identity, Azure and cloud, Exchange Server, Dynamics and Xbox. Only one bug is under active attack and none is publicly known. ZDI says that doesn’t mean less exploitation, only fewer zero-days, and it guesses that AI is better at reversing patches than at finding and exploiting bugs in closed-source software.

The exploited bug is CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing flaw, and its name undersells the impact. An attacker sends a crafted message file and talks the user into opening it, and Outlook connects to an attacker-controlled location without the usual external-content warning, which leaks the user’s NTLMv2 hash.

“An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook. Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. Exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction.” reads the advisory. “An attacker must send a user a malicious Office file and convince them to open it.”

The attacker can then authenticate as that user. The Preview Pane isn’t an attack path and the CVSS score is only 6.5, but ZDI says to put it first because Microsoft marks it as exploited.

CVE-2026-116928 is a Windows Search remote code execution bug reached through Exchange Server. An unauthenticated attacker emails a crafted attachment, and the bug triggers when the server indexes it automatically, so the recipient never opens anything. It’s zero-click, scores CVSS 9.8, and ZDI rates it more severe than any of the nine patches Exchange gets this month.

CVE-2026-119958 hits the Windows LDAP service. An unauthenticated attacker sends crafted LDAP calls over the network, triggers an out-of-bounds write and runs code in the service context, which could be destructive on domain controllers. ZDI says to test and deploy it quickly. CVE-2026-119952, a Schannel remote code execution flaw, is marked “Exploitation More Likely”, one of only a few Critical patches with that rating, and its high attack complexity is why the score is lower.

CVE-2026-119990, an Azure OpenAI elevation of privilege bug, got a bulletin that said “Customer Action Required: Yes” and then listed nothing to do. An unauthenticated attacker could send a crafted request over the internet and reach orchestration information, change workflows or disrupt the service. Microsoft has since revised it to say no customer action is needed. A bulletin that says action required and lists none is the most relaxed urgent notice you’ll read this month.

Two more stand out for their components. CVE-2026-95962 is a use-after-free in the little-documented Windows Virtual Filtering Platform, reachable with a crafted network packet and needing no authentication or user interaction. It involves a race condition, but ZDI notes those get beaten all the time at Pwn2Own. CVE-2026-112967 is a heap overflow in the Xbox Live Networking Service with a CVSS of 9.8, and ZDI doesn’t think exploitation is likely but enjoys imagining Xbox Live exploits in the wild.

ZDI counts 30 wormable bugs this month, down from 59 last month. Seventeen carry advisory wording about an unauthenticated attacker running code over the network with no interaction, and 13 use variant wording or have no FAQ but show the same pattern in their summaries and CVSS vectors. ZDI warns it may be wrong on some, since a few advisories are light on detail.

Network-facing services like DNS, DHCP, LDAP and Exchange deserve the earliest attention.

Title: Threat Actors Exploit Openwave, Cisco BroadWorks Vulnerabilities
Context: An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted XML message to the Open Client Interface – Provisioning (OCI-P) service,” Cisco notes in its advisory
Full Text:
Threat actors are exploiting two vulnerabilities in Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder and Cisco BroadWorks to access sensitive information.

Openwave Messaging provides email and messaging platforms, including webmail, to communication service providers. Webtop Media Transcoder handles document conversion, and Openwave’s advisory ties it to the company’s webmail.

The Webtop Media Transcoder bug, tracked as CVE-2026-111793, exists because administrator-defined file-type restrictions are not enforced, allowing users to convert unintended file types.

“This may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the webmail experience,” Openwave Messaging explains in an advisory.

Webtop Media Transcoder version 1.1.22.0, which rolled out in December 2021, contains patches. The security defect was disclosed on October 7, and a CVE record was published on October 16.

Japan JVN flagged the weakness as exploited on November 9, warning that an authenticated attacker could exploit it to upload a specially crafted file and obtain sensitive information.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

The Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20320, was disclosed on August 19 as an out-of-band blind XML external entity injection that could be exploited remotely, without authentication, to read sensitive configuration information.

“This vulnerability exists because XML entries are improperly parsed due to external entity resolution being allowed by default. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted XML message to the Open Client Interface – Provisioning (OCI-P) service,” Cisco notes in its advisory.

Patches for the issue were included in version RI.2026.07 of BroadWorks Application Delivery Platform, Application Server, Profile Server, and Xtended Services Platform.

On November 8, Malbear Labs warned that a Chinese-speaking threat actor has been exploiting the vulnerability in a broad campaign that relied on an autonomous AI intrusion harness to target a European telecommunications provider and its customers.

At least 13 organizations using the telecoms provider’s services may have been targeted. The campaign focused on asset enumeration, credential theft, and subscriber billing and device records harvesting.

The US cybersecurity agency CISA added the Openwave and Cisco security defects to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on November 10, urging federal agencies to patch both by November 24.

Additionally, CISA expanded the KEV list with two Barracuda flaws, an Outlook zero-day patched on Tuesday, and a Chrome bug patched on November 9 as a zero-day.

Title: Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes
Context: Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs
Full Text:
Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws.

These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers. More than 500 flaws relate to elevation of privilege, followed by remote code execution and information disclosure bugs.

With the latest round of fixes, Microsoft has addressed over 5,100 CVEs this year alone, according to Satnam Narang, senior staff research engineer at Tenable.

Of these, a Moderate-severity security flaw in Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2026-124194, CVSS score: 6.5) has been flagged as actively exploited by Microsoft.

"Product UI does not warn users of unsafe actions in Microsoft Office Outlook allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network," Microsoft said in an advisory.

An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and persuade a target to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook.

This, in turn, could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information, such as an NTLMv2 hash, that could be used to impersonate the user.

Microsoft emphasized that successful exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction. The tech giant credited a researcher named Nono and Anthropic's Benoît Sevens (using Claude) with discovering and reporting the flaw.

"Email is the easiest door into any company, and this flaw turns one opened file into a stolen identity," Jack Bicer, director of vulnerability research at Action1, said. "A captured hash can let an attacker sign in as the victim, read their data, and move to other systems they can reach."

"The Moderate label undersells this one. Attackers are already exploiting it, it needs only one click on an email file, and it hits Outlook, which nearly every organization runs. A stolen hash can open doors far beyond the inbox."

That said, Redmond has not attributed the activity to a particular threat actor or provided technical details on how the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild. The advisory also doesn't spell out whether the discovery came before or after attackers began exploiting the flaw.

The development has prompted the U.S. U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to add the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, requiring federal agencies to apply the fix by November 24, 2026.

Some other vulnerabilities of note include a number of remote code execution flaws impacting Windows Search (CVE-2026-116928), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (CVE-2026-119958), Windows Schannel (CVE-2026-119952), Windows Virtual Filtering Platform (CVE-2026-95962), and Windows Xbox Live Networking Service (CVE-2026-112967), as well as a privilege escalation flaw in Azure OpenAI (CVE-2026-119990).

"Most security teams haven't quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and '2shell'-branded everything, and we're yet again at another Patch Tuesday," Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at watchTowr, said.

"Teams are really starting to feel the strain of working out 'what actually matters?' when there is fire after fire every day demanding immediate attention. Start with what you actually have exposed to the Internet, then what’s already being exploited in the wild, and only then everything else. Before going into panic mode, check whether you even use the vulnerable component, or meet the prerequisites for exploitation."

Title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
Context: (Fixed in October 2026) The addition of CVE-2026-111793 to the KEV catalog follows an alert issued by Japan Vulnerability Notes (JPN), which noted in an advisory that the...
Full Text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Tuesday added two security flaws impacting Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.

Details of the vulnerabilities are below -

CVE-2026-20320 (CVSS score: 7.5) - An improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability in the Open Client Interface (OCI) XML Parser of Cisco BroadWorks that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system with the privileges of the Cisco BroadWorks user. (Fixed in August 2026)

CVE-2026-111793 (CVSS score: 4.3) - An incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability in Openwave Messaging Webtop Media Transcoder that could allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience. (Fixed in October 2026)

The addition of CVE-2026-111793 to the KEV catalog follows an alert issued by Japan Vulnerability Notes (JPN), which noted in an advisory that the "developer states that attacks exploiting the vulnerability have been observed."

The vulnerability information portal also warned that an authenticated attacker could exploit the vulnerability to upload a specially crafted file and obtain sensitive information.

As for CVE-2026-20320, the security defect has been put to use as part of an agentic attack campaign dubbed Operation Snowball in which an unknown Chinese-speaking threat actor leveraged an autonomous framework built using a jailbroken version of the DeepSeek Flash model to target a European telecom provider and 13 companies hosted on its infrastructure.

The activity resulted in the enumeration of hundreds of assets, extraction of dozens of credential sets, and exfiltration of thousands of rows of subscriber billing and device records from the provider's internal billing platform over a two-week period, according to Malbear Labs.

The AI agent has capabilities to exploit a portfolio of known security vulnerabilities spanning a wide range of products, including -

JBoss RichFaces (CVE-2013-2165)

Liferay CE/DXP (CVE-2020-7961)

ForgeRock OpenAM (CVE-2021-35464)

Linux (CVE-2021-4034)

SAP NetWeaver (CVE-2022-22536)

Cisco Expressway (CVE-2023-20269)

Citrix NetScaler(CVE-2023-4966)

Qlik Sense (CVE-2023-41265, CVE-2023-41266)

PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CVE-2024-3400, CVE-2024-9474)

Adobe Experience Manager (CVE-2025-54249)

Broadcom VMware Cloud Director (CVE-2026-2003, CVE-2026-2004, CVE-2026-2005, CVE-2026-2006)

Claris FileMaker Server (CVE-2026-86934), and

F5 BIG-IP (CVE-2026-41225)

"The primary target on the telecommunications provider's infrastructure was the BroadWorks XSP (eXtended Services Platform), Release 23.0.1.1075, running on port 2208," Malbear Labs said. "The agent exploited CVE-2026-20320, an unauthenticated XXE in the BroadWorks OCI XML parser."

"From the XSP host, the agent recovered the system identity private key, three SSL credential sets, and three additional private keys with certificate matches confirmed. The system identity key is used by the BroadWorks platform to authenticate between its own components; possessing it allows impersonation of the XSP in inter-component communication."

The activity has also been characterized by the use of reconnaissance tools, Sliver for post-exploitation, Chisel, along with web shells like Behinder for persistent access.

"This is a threat actor who delegated the intrusion to an AI and checked in asynchronously to review progress," Malbear Labs added. The primary agent ran continuously, issued parallel tasks to worker agents, maintained a coherent operational plan across the full campaign, and adapted to defensive controls without pausing for operator input."

"The harness ran the reconnaissance, identified the attack surface, chose the exploitation path, adapted when controls blocked it, wrote new tools when existing ones failed, extracted credentials, exfiltrated data, and compiled a finished target list, all without the operator present during any of it."

Late last month, Cisco revealed that two different vulnerabilities in Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20127, CVSS score: 10.0) Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software (CVE-2026-76418, CVSS score: 8.6) have been actively exploited in the wild.

In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the patches by November 24, 2026, to secure their networks.

Title: Able2Shell: Frequently asked questions for reported N-able N-central zero-day vulnerabilities
Context: As of November 10, there are no details available for any threat actor activity connected to Able2Shell exploitation
Full Text:
N-able released a hotfix for N-central that fixes seven CVEs after a researcher published proof-of-concept code for 33 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities. The researcher says one attack chain needs no credentials.

Key Takeaways

Able2Shell is a set of 33 alleged vulnerabilities in N-able N-central, published with proof-of-concept code. The researcher says one chain lets an unauthenticated attacker run commands on the server.

Security firms report exploitation attempts against N-central honeypots, but as of November 10, no confirmed compromise of a customer server has been reported.

N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 on November 10. It fixes seven CVEs.

Background

Tenable's Research Special Operations (RSO) team has compiled this blog to answer Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) regarding Able2Shell, a set of reported zero-day vulnerabilities in N-able N-central.

FAQ

When was Able2Shell first disclosed?

A researcher operating under the GitHub account “Oracle-Security” published a write-up titled “Able2Shell” in the account’s CVEs repository. It describes 33 alleged N-central vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept code. The earliest README commit is dated November 9, 2026 at 04:14 UTC. N-able described the release as a public disclosure by an independent security researcher. N-able does not state whether it was notified in advance and does not name the researcher.

What are the vulnerabilities associated with Able2Shell?

On November 10, N-able published seven CVE records for vulnerabilities fixed in N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2. On its status page, N-able says the release addresses “the most critical November 9 vulnerabilities” and that a follow-up hotfix will provide further security updates. The page lists all seven as related CVEs. One, CVE-2026-91000, had been reserved on September 14, before the public Able2Shell disclosure.

CVE

Description (per N-able)

CVSSv4

CVE-2026-125883

Multiple XML external entity (XXE) vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125881

Schema-hint server-side request forgery (SSRF) via service import schema validation

CVE-2026-91000

Insecure IPC channels lead to local privilege escalation

8.4

CVE-2026-125880

Stored cross-site scripting (XSS) via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)

8.3

N-able’s CVE titles match several finding types in the researcher’s README, but N-able has not said which of the 33 findings each CVE addresses. N-able credits CVE-2026-125882 to Nate Fair of Sprocket Security, and a file repository path traversal also appears in the README.

Is Able2Shell one vulnerability or several?

Several. The README lists 33 findings, and some of them are steps in longer exploit chains built from other entries on the same list. The researcher lists four exploit chains. The rest are standalone findings.

Chain

Login needed
